solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Roam splendid rambling area offering all one could want

definitions.text: area offering all one could want

indicators.note: rambling describes wandering about aimlessly, so the letters of the two words before it wander into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to wander a lovely stretch of countryside that seems to have everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' reads as country walking after 'Roam', but it signals that ROAM SPLENDID is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical land promised to Abraham's descendants is used figuratively for any place of perfect fulfilment.

clue.text: Teesside racecourse, favourite for VIP treatment

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town on Teesside in north-east England with a horse-racing course
a favourite, especially a teacher's favourite, is a pet

explanation.surface: A racegoer at a northern English course has a fancied horse and wants star treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a racecourse town in north-east England. 'favourite' sounds like a betting favourite, but here it is a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dignitaries are welcomed by rolling out a crimson carpet, so the phrase means lavish ceremonial welcome.

clue.text: Large lizard egg found in upland area

indicators.note: something found in a place sits within it, so the egg goes inside the upland area

parts.note: a moor is open upland ground
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A naturalist discovers an egg on the high moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is usually O in crosswords, but here it is a louse's egg; 'found in' puts it inside the upland word.
explanation.definitionFit: Monitors are a genus of big reptiles, including the Komodo dragon, so the word names a sizeable lizard.

clue.text: A joiner fighting in the army, one going with fortitude

indicators.note: one going means it departs, so a single letter for one leaves the soldiering

parts.note: serving as a soldier is soldiering
I is the Roman numeral for one
iron, as in an iron will, means strength of character

explanation.surface: A carpenter who joined up and had to show courage in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' takes I out of SOLDIERING to leave SOLDERING. A joiner reads as a carpenter, but here it is a tool that joins metal.
explanation.definitionFit: This heated tool melts solder to fuse metal parts together, so it is literally something that joins.

clue.text: Devil in protest over the ending of sin

indicators.note: in a down clue the protest sits over, above, the following letter

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or rally

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, here of sin

explanation.surface: The devil is out protesting against the end of sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit, and the devil is the chief of them; they are synonyms in everyday speech.

clue.text: State of unrest in Cappadocia

indicators.note: the letters needed lie in the middle of the place name Cappadocia

explanation.surface: Turmoil in an ancient region of Anatolia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado is fuss or commotion, a state of bustle and agitation.

clue.text: Note great annoyance where such hazard is created?

definitions.text: Note great annoyance where such hazard is created?

parts.note: D is a musical note
anger is strong annoyance

explanation.surface: Musing that a hazard arises wherever real fury is noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: D plus ANGER, and anger is where such peril arises.
explanation.definitionFit: Danger is a hazard or risk, and the clue suggests rage is exactly what produces peril.

clue.text: About to exploit something deserving of support

parts.note: ca. is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about
to exploit is to use

explanation.surface: Someone is about to take advantage of a worthy charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'going to', but 'About' is CA on its own and 'to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause is a principle or movement that people back and campaign for.

clue.text: An accessory nowadays put on

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era of years
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Someone puts on the latest fashionable trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra item attached to something, much as an accessory supplements an outfit or machine.

clue.text: Ridicule a parliamentarian taken in by an idiot

indicators.note: being taken in by someone puts you within them, so the parliamentarian goes inside the idiot

parts.note: a loon is a crazy or foolish person
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is fooled by a simpleton, and is mocked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' suggests being deceived, but it is a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon is to satirise or mock publicly, the same as to ridicule.

clue.text: Put down roots outside a West Coast City

indicators.note: the roots word goes outside, around, the letter a

parts.note: to settle is to make a permanent home somewhere

explanation.surface: Advice to settle in a city on America's Pacific coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State on the Pacific seaboard of the USA.

clue.text: Count, say, number to enjoy life either side of fifty

indicators.note: the two letters for living go one on each side of the Roman fifty

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An aristocrat in his fifties determined to live it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb with 'number', but it is the title, and 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is one rank of the titled aristocracy, an instance of the peerage class.

clue.text: Pottery linked to low quality which is played out in court

definitions.text: which is played out in court

indicators.note: the pottery word comes linked after the poor-quality word, so the two are joined in that order

parts.note: something bad is of poor standard
Minton is a famous English ceramics maker from Stoke-on-Trent

explanation.surface: Cheap pottery involved in a dispute heard by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: MINTON is a Staffordshire maker of fine china. 'court' suggests law, but this court is a sports court.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played on a netted indoor court, so it is literally played out there.

clue.text: Allowed for each glove being cut down initially

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head

indicators.note: a word that is cut loses its tail, here the final letter of the glove

parts.note: a mitten is a glove without separate fingers

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of down

explanation.surface: A glove may be trimmed down for each wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut' removes N from MITTEN to give MITTE; 'initially' gives D from 'down'.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitted means authorised or given leave, the same as allowed.

clue.text: Finished in the endless long grass

indicators.note: the little word the loses its end letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
in golf the rough is the long grass beside the fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer's round ends with the ball lost in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The ROUGH is golf's long grass off the fairway; 'endless' trims THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To be through is to be done or finished, as in 'I'm through with this'.

clue.text: Completely defeated and told where to go

definitions.meaning: an army that is beaten and put to flight has been crushed
sent along a set course or path, as with traffic or parcels

explanation.surface: A beaten side is shown the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'shouted', the other with 'booted' in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is utterly beaten in battle; the other is directed along a particular way.

clue.text: Talk about right plan

indicators.note: the talk word goes about, around, the letter for right

parts.note: to chat is to talk informally

explanation.surface: Discussion of the correct strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart is a map or diagram, and as a verb to chart a course is to plan it.

clue.text: Frequently one's upset about Financial Times

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the newspaper's initials
upset means overturned or disturbed, so the letters of one are jumbled

parts.note: FT is the usual short name for the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is regularly put out by what the business paper reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes OEN from ONE, which goes 'about' FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and frequently are direct synonyms: many times, repeatedly.

clue.text: Saw half of explosion going up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
half of the ten-letter word for a blast is its first five letters

parts.note: a detonation is an explosion

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed a blast as it went up.
explanation.walkthrough: DETON, the first half of DETONATION, is read upwards. 'going up' suggests the blast, but it reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe or notice it, so noted means saw.

clue.text: Sharing making alterations to dress

indicators.note: alterations change something's form, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people share a dress that needs taking in by a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making alterations to dress' sounds like tailoring, but 'dress' is the definition, as in dressing food.
explanation.definitionFit: To garnish is to decorate a dish, just as one dresses a salad.

clue.text: Rubbish wagon reversing for farm vehicle

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so the combined letters are read from the end

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
a cart is a simple wagon

explanation.surface: A refuse lorry backs up to make way for a farm vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish wagon' looks like a bin lorry, but the two words are clued separately and 'reversing' turns both round together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is the powerful vehicle used on farms to pull ploughs and trailers.

clue.text: Grow old and wise — not the first

indicators.note: the first letter of the wise word is dropped

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: Getting older and wiser, though not top of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older, the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Complete roadside channel that's not been started

indicators.note: something not started lacks its beginning, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: a gutter is the drainage channel at the edge of a road

explanation.surface: A drain beside the road that is finished but was never begun.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means total or absolute, as in utter nonsense: complete.

clue.text: Fine porcelain unusually enriched with sand

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters of the two words are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: A fine ceramic oddly strengthened with sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen porcelain, made near Dresden in Saxony, is famous delicate chinaware.
